content.text: All indemnity language sits in § 20 and meets the preferred checklist in full.

input.quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
input.rationale: § 20 satisfies the preferred position in full: Vendor expressly defends, indemnifies and holds harmless Customer and its Affiliates against third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims relating to the Services or Deliverables (20.1), and against claims arising from Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud (20.2). Standard procedure is present — prompt notice, reasonable cooperation (at the indemnifying Party's expense) and control of the defence, with a settlement-consent protection (20.4). Customer's reciprocal indemnity is properly narrow, covering only unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorized and Customer's violation of Applicable Law, with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modification, combination or instructions (20.3). Beyond the preferred level, 20.5 adds procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and § 21.3 treats indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims outside the liability cap, which is better for us than the fallback 3× super-cap. No redline required.
